sentences.text: 2. It is submitted by counsel for applicant that applicant had lodged an FIR for offence under Sections 498A, 294, 323/34, 506 Part II of IPC and sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and respondent and her in-laws were prosecuted in RCT No. 518/2023.

However, by judgment dated 14.10.2024, all her in-laws including respondent were acquitted of the charge under Sections 498A,
294, 323/34, 506 Part 2 of IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
Similarly, applicant had filed an application under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C which too was dismissed by order dated 09.12.2023 on the basis of compromise.

It is submitted that so far as criminal case is concerned,
applicant had turned hostile on the assurance given by her in-laws.
Similarly, application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C was also dismissed on the basis of compromise.

The applicant tried her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18248 2 MCC-660-2025 level best to save her marital life but by playing fraud on the applicant, the respondent and her in-laws had successfully got an order of acquittal for offences under Sections 498A, 294, 323/34, 506 Part 2 and 498A of the IPC and Sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act as well as they successfully got the application filed under Section 125 of the Cr.P.C dismissed.

It is submitted that the behaviour of the respondents did not improve and accordingly she has once again lodged an FIR against the respondents and in-laws for offences under Sections 85, 296, 115(2), 351(3) and 3(5) of the BNS and under Section 3/4 of the Smt. It is submitted that applicant has to look after her minor child aged about 3 years and therefore it would be very inconvenient for the applicant to attend the court proceedings at Morena and thus it is prayed that Case No. 158/2023 (HMA) pending in the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Morena may be transferred to the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court,
Chhatarpur.

sentences.text: 3 . Per contra , the application is vehemently opposed by counsel for the respondents.
It is submitted by counsel for respondent that respondent is suffering from 42% of locomotor disability, therefore it would be difficult for him to attend the proceedings at Chhatarpur.

It is further submitted that respondent has lodged an FIR in Crime No. 318/2025 at Police Station Kotwali, District Morena for offences under Sections 115(2), 296, 3(5) and 351(2) of the BNS, 2023 on the ground that on 14.05.2025 at about 3:30 p.m., when respondent and his younger brother were returning after attending the court proceedings, then applicant and her father and brother scolded him as to why he had filed an application for divorce and when he replied that since the applicant is not residing in her matrimonial house and is unnecessarily harassing him, therefore, he has filed the application for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:18248 3 MCC-660-2025 divorce
, then he was slapped by all the three persons.
It is submitted that in case the case proceedings are transferred to Chhatarpur, then there is every possibility that his safety may be in jeopardy.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
5. Respondent has not denied the fact that applicant is looking after her 3 years old child.

It is the case of applicant that by giving false assurance the respondent as well as his family successfully got the criminal case dismissed as well as also got the proceedings under section 125 of Cr.P.C dismissed, but thereafter their conduct and behaviour did not improve.
Applicant has filed copy of judgment of acquittal from offences under Sections 498A, 294, 323/34, 506 Part II of the IPC and under Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
From plain reading of the said judgment it is clear that applicant had turned hostile.
Applicant has also filed copy of order dated 09.12.2023 by which the application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C was dismissed on the ground of compromise.

Therefore, it is clear that applicant had tried her level best to save her marital life and therefore, for the time being it cannot be said that the security of respondent would be in jeopardy in case he is required to attend the case at Chhatarpur.
Furthermore, RCT No. 518/2023 was decided by JMFC, Bijavar, District Chhatarpur and similarly proceedings under Section 125 Cr.P.C had also taken place in Chhatarpur.
It is not the case of respondent that he was ever maltreated or threatened or beaten by the applicant at Chhatarpur.

6. Under these circumstances, where the applicant is required to maintain her minor child aged about 3 years and looking to the bad blood between the parties where both the parties are lodging FIRs against each other, this Court is of considered opinion that it would not be in the fitness of things to compel the applicant to attend the proceedings at Morena.

2 7.

Accordingly, it is held that it is a fit case where Case No. 158/2023 (HMA) pending in the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Morena should be transferred to the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Chhatarpur.
